episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose the recommendation project and use one rehearsal comparison to explain what the exported discussion preserves, what remains only live, and how to recover if storage fails.

concepts.experiment: Compare the recommendation mission card with the ring card, then select the retailer project and inspect its stakeholder and boundary.
concepts.evidence: Identify the difference between one ranking endpoint and its separate development host; neither choosing CloudML nor selecting a card establishes readiness.
concepts.transfer_question: When would the ring project be a better context for the question being investigated?

concepts.experiment: Predict a labeled interface-practice outcome, pin a baseline, capture a contrast, then move the live control again.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which display changes and which captured comparison remains fixed; these practice cases establish interface behavior, not ranking performance.
concepts.transfer_question: When should you capture a new contrast rather than rely on the earlier one?

concepts.experiment: Save and read back a rehearsal record, then exercise the storage-unavailable case and download fallback.
concepts.evidence: Compare live session state, acknowledged stored content, and the downloaded artifact; persistence must be demonstrated rather than inferred from a green display.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a downloaded record be necessary even after a successful save?

concepts.experiment: Inspect the rehearsal discussion and choose which captured comparison to include in the first handoff.
concepts.evidence: Check that project identity, prediction, actual contrast, and next question survive export; an export is an investigation record, not a release certificate.
concepts.transfer_question: When would the instructor need a different captured comparison to understand your decision?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Recommend the first investigation for the missing-new-products problem: cite saved behavioral and execution evidence, reject one tempting alternative, and state what finding would reverse your recommendation.

concepts.experiment: Change the supplied mix of established and newly listed products while holding the ranker and runtime fixed; reveal independently labeled outcomes where available.
concepts.evidence: Compare operational health with new-item exposure and task outcomes, keeping unsupported slices unknown rather than treating absent complaints as success.
concepts.transfer_question: When would execution optimization become more urgent than gathering new-item evidence?

concepts.experiment: On the same complete ranking-request breakdown, compare faster dense arithmetic with a supported feature or embedding movement intervention.
concepts.evidence: Inspect the changed stage beside untouched lookup, transfer, and filtering time; an unpriced counterfactual remains an incomplete purchasing recommendation.
concepts.transfer_question: When would the arithmetic intervention become the better choice?

concepts.experiment: Compare supplied ID-only and content-aware candidates against separate ranking-quality, new-item coverage, request-time, and memory obligations.
concepts.evidence: Retain failed and unknown gates visibly; better average relevance cannot compensate for excluding required new products or exceeding a resource limit. Include endpoint energy as its own supplied gate; retain unknown energy evidence explicitly.
concepts.transfer_question: When would retaining the simpler candidate be preferable?

concepts.experiment: On the separate development host, compare supported reductions in interaction examples, work per example, and realized execution time.
concepts.evidence: Inspect work and time separately from matched ranking outcomes; fewer interactions may remove sparse new-item or seller evidence.
concepts.transfer_question: When would reducing work per example be safer than reducing the training pool?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose a host/accelerator placement or hold using saved locality, fit, and operating evidence; reject another placement and name the requirement that would reverse your choice.

concepts.experiment: Move a supported ranking stage between the endpoint host and accelerator, varying the declared candidate payload or same-host transfer path.
concepts.evidence: Compare complete transfer-plus-execution time with an ideal-accelerator bound; do not insert WAN propagation into this same-host comparison.
concepts.transfer_question: When would keeping the stage on the host beat accelerator offload?

concepts.experiment: At fixed candidates and features, compare more arithmetic capacity with a supported working-memory or bandwidth repair.
concepts.evidence: Inspect separate embedding residency, live feature buffers, traffic, and runtime; a nonfitting placement has no executable timing claim.
concepts.transfer_question: When would bandwidth rather than additional capacity become the useful purchase?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported endpoint operating policies under a declared node-energy allowance while retaining useful request service.
concepts.evidence: Inspect useful completed service, node operating energy, and sustained power separately; a powered endpoint has no invented ring-style battery.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a more energy-consuming policy be required to preserve service?

concepts.experiment: Use saved placement comparisons and change one feature/data-access permission or transfer requirement before explicitly selecting host, accelerator, partitioned execution, or hold.
concepts.evidence: Inspect surviving gates, local work, transfer costs, artifact compatibility, and unknown task evidence; moving stages does not supply missing new-item history.
concepts.transfer_question: When would partitioning lose its advantage over keeping the complete path on one processor?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Update the project contract for newly listed products, identify the artifacts and owners affected, and use saved checks to justify a repair or hold with a reversal condition.

concepts.experiment: Add the requirement that eligible new products must have a supported content-based path, then mark affected data, feature, candidate, model, and evaluation artifacts.
concepts.evidence: Compare necessary revisions with preserved artifacts; packaging alone cannot repair missing features, while rebuilding unchanged components adds avoidable work.
concepts.transfer_question: When would preserving the old ranker behind a restricted contract be acceptable?

concepts.experiment: Move discovery of the same unsupported-feature defect between development stages in a fixed dependency timeline.
concepts.evidence: Compare early-check effort with downstream repair work and elapsed schedule; the same defect can incur different rework without changing its cause.
concepts.transfer_question: When would an expensive early target check cease to repay its cost?

concepts.experiment: Select a release evidence bundle, apply a supported feature-path repair, and rerun the affected gate on the identified package.
concepts.evidence: Distinguish detected failure, repaired but unverified, missing new-item outcomes, and passing compatible evidence.
concepts.transfer_question: When would keeping the baseline be preferable to releasing the repaired candidate?

concepts.experiment: Replay an early new-item exposure warning followed by delayed outcome observations, choosing the owner and next evidence request.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which population each signal covers; seller complaints and changed input statistics do not establish population-wide harm or successful repair.
concepts.transfer_question: When would requesting broader outcomes be preferable to immediately retraining?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose a data repair for the cold-start pipeline using saved comparisons, explain the alternative you reject, and identify what evidence would change the repair priority.

concepts.experiment: Allocate a fixed review effort between broad relevance labeling and adjudicating ambiguous new-item/session judgments; compare a supplied revised rubric.
concepts.evidence: Inspect disagreement and changed target definitions without rewriting model predictions; consistency is not proof that the rubric captures useful discovery.
concepts.transfer_question: When would targeted adjudication be more valuable than labeling more sessions?

concepts.experiment: Compare record versus session/entity/time-aware splits, then fit feature state on training data versus before splitting and replay request-time snapshots.
concepts.evidence: Inspect leakage from later purchases and incompatible feature transforms; a favorable leaked score is not improved future-session behavior.
concepts.transfer_question: When could a simpler split support the specific claim without contaminating it?

concepts.experiment: Keep candidate and feature semantics fixed while changing a supported storage representation or read/decode/transform stage.
concepts.evidence: Inspect delivered examples and consumer demand beside storage and preparation costs; compressed features can save bytes while adding decode work.
concepts.transfer_question: When would materializing a larger representation improve the complete development path?

concepts.experiment: Replay a product-feature semantic violation, quarantine or repair it, and trace affected training and endpoint descendants; compare a benign catalog-mixture alert.
concepts.evidence: Inspect schema validity, semantic checks, lineage, lost usable data, and unresolved ranking outcomes rather than interpreting every alert as harm.
concepts.transfer_question: When would monitoring without quarantine be the better response?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Select a feasible ranking-computation envelope using saved topology, differentiation, phase-state, and batching comparisons; explain its limit and the change that would favor another envelope.

concepts.experiment: Change supported ranker width or depth and inspect layer shapes; contrast a linear stack with the supplied nonlinear ranking dependency.
concepts.evidence: Compare parameters, arithmetic, and activations without assuming larger capacity improves new-item ranking or that extra linear layers add the required expressivity.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a narrower nonlinear candidate be preferable to a wider linear one?

concepts.experiment: In a small ranking-layer dependency graph, discard or retain a forward activation needed for a weight gradient.
concepts.evidence: Inspect whether the derivative remains computable and which value must be restored; absent dependency state is not a zero gradient.
concepts.transfer_question: When would retaining a forward value be preferable to regenerating it?

concepts.experiment: Compare inference and development-host training allocations for the same exact ranker and embedding configuration while varying batch size.
concepts.evidence: Inspect weights, activations, gradients, and optimizer state separately; endpoint inference fit does not establish training fit.
concepts.transfer_question: When would restricting trainable scope be worth investigating rather than changing endpoint hardware?

concepts.experiment: Grow a supported development or controlled-execution batch at fixed ranker and candidate shape.
concepts.evidence: Compare weight traffic per example and arithmetic intensity with live activation capacity; keep this reuse experiment distinct from arrival-based serving policy.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a smaller batch be the only useful executable choice?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose a task-supported ranking architecture or request missing evidence, citing saved native comparisons and explicitly separating conclusions from the language reference study.

concepts.experiment: Compare supplied ID-only, content-feature, and hybrid rankers under established-item and new-item requirements and supported feature transformations.
concepts.evidence: Inspect matched relevance and cold-start coverage alongside structural assumptions; an ID representation cannot learn an unseen product from a larger table alone.
concepts.transfer_question: When would an ID-only candidate be preferable to the content-aware alternative?

concepts.experiment: Trace dense scoring, candidate-feature movement, and irregular embedding lookup for controlled native architecture cases.
concepts.evidence: Compare arithmetic, traffic, and resident-state signatures; a dense arithmetic improvement may leave irregular lookup binding.
concepts.transfer_question: When would reducing embedding traffic be more useful than adding dense compute?

concepts.experiment: Open the separately named language reference; compare materialized and unmaterialized attention scores at fixed history, then prefill and decode.
concepts.evidence: Inspect retained state beside unchanged dense score arithmetic and phase-specific work; these are reference observations, not evidence for the native ranker or its embeddings.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a storage-saving attention path help despite unchanged dense arithmetic?

concepts.experiment: Vary the supported product-vocabulary or embedding-table envelope while holding requested rows fixed.
concepts.evidence: Inspect table capacity separately from per-request access and supplied new-item outcomes; adding IDs creates neither interaction history nor useful learned representations.
concepts.transfer_question: When would expanding capacity be preferable to adding a content-feature fallback?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose an execution plan for the ranking path using saved dispatch, setup, differentiation, and compatibility evidence; reject one plan and specify its reversal condition.

concepts.experiment: Compare eager calls, a captured ranking region, and supported fusion on the same required graph.
concepts.evidence: Inspect launch overhead and intermediate feature/tensor traffic separately; preserve lookup, eligibility, and filtering instead of deleting them to make the graph faster.
concepts.transfer_question: When would retaining eager boundaries be worth the extra overhead?

concepts.experiment: Change graph reuse horizon and candidate-shape or feature-signature churn for the same ranking semantics.
concepts.evidence: Compare compilation/setup with cumulative runtime savings; a faster warm invocation can still lose over the supported operating horizon.
concepts.transfer_question: When would compilation become preferable to eager execution?

concepts.experiment: On the development host, revisit the ranking gradient graph and compare retaining versus supported regeneration of saved forward values.
concepts.evidence: Inspect dependency validity, saved-state allocation, and recomputation work; automatic differentiation does not eliminate the required values.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a more state-intensive saved-value policy be preferable?

concepts.experiment: Compare native operator support, explicit host/accelerator partitioning, accounted fallback, and rejected export for the exact ranking graph and shapes.
concepts.evidence: Inspect required operations and boundary costs; a successful export that omits eligibility or feature transformation changes the task.
concepts.transfer_question: When would rejecting export be preferable to accepting fallback?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose a development-host training recipe or hold, using saved state and matched progress evidence to explain the binding term, rejected repair, and reversal condition.

concepts.experiment: Compare supported full adaptation with restricted embedding/ranker adaptation while showing each training allocation.
concepts.evidence: Inspect weights, gradients, optimizer state, and retained activations separately; freezing a component need not remove its forward or backward dependencies.
concepts.transfer_question: When would full adaptation justify its extra state?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported resident-batch, micro-batch/accumulation, and recomputation recipes at the same declared effective batch where valid.
concepts.evidence: Inspect fit, repeated execution, and recipe equivalence; a matching batch label alone does not establish identical optimization behavior.
concepts.transfer_question: When would spending more memory be preferable to accumulation or recomputation?

concepts.experiment: Reveal supplied matched learning progress for supported precision recipes against the same relevance and new-item targets.
concepts.evidence: Compare step time with observed target attainment, preserving failure and missing target evidence rather than generating quality from speed.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a slower numerical recipe be the better development choice?

concepts.experiment: Inspect a partially revealed development-host profile, try a tempting ineffective intervention, then test a supported repair of the binding stage.
concepts.evidence: Compare useful training work, input/lookup/compute timing, and achieved target progress; high GPU busy time does not establish productive learning.
concepts.transfer_question: When would improving data preparation cease to be the priority?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose a training-data policy using saved learning, coverage, complete-campaign, and data-path evidence; reject one alternative and state when selection should be abandoned or refreshed.

concepts.experiment: Allocate the same supported training work among repeated interactions, novel sparse/new-item cases, and a supported model/data balance pilot.
concepts.evidence: Inspect work-matched ranking progress and target attainment; early learning gain does not guarantee the final target or represent unseen items.
concepts.transfer_question: When would repeating existing interactions be preferable to acquiring novel cases?

concepts.experiment: Select a finite interaction subset under justified item, seller, session, and new-item coverage floors.
concepts.evidence: Inspect displaced high-scoring records and infeasible floors or deficient eligible pools; counts alone do not establish useful outcomes for those conditions.
concepts.transfer_question: When would preserving a coverage floor outweigh selecting the highest-scored records?

concepts.experiment: Compare selection policies while charging scorer preparation, archive scoring, feature preparation, refresh, and training over the supported reuse horizon.
concepts.evidence: Inspect complete campaign work and time at matched accepted quality; exposure-conditioned records and stale rankings limit reuse.
concepts.transfer_question: When would retaining the full pool be cheaper than selecting a subset?

concepts.experiment: Keep selected interaction identities fixed and compare full-stream discard, scattered access, and a materialized subset.
concepts.evidence: Inspect actual reads, preparation, extra storage, and the critical path; fewer trained examples need not eliminate full archive scans.
concepts.transfer_question: When would repacking the subset repay its extra preparation and storage?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose an exact executable ranking bundle or hold using saved resource and matched outcome evidence; explain a rejected compression path and the condition that would reverse the choice.

concepts.experiment: Change a supported ranker/embedding representation while keeping checkpoint bytes, resident weights, live feature buffers, and runtime allocations distinct.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which allocation changes and which still fails; a smaller stored bundle may leave candidate-buffer capacity binding.
concepts.transfer_question: When would reducing live candidate state be preferable to compressing weights?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported post-training and training-aware numerical artifacts using matched calibration and held-out established/new-item cases.
concepts.evidence: Inspect ranking relevance, required coverage, and preparation cost, retaining absent quality evidence; a technique name guarantees no recovery.
concepts.transfer_question: When would paying for training-aware preparation be preferable to retaining a wider artifact?

concepts.experiment: Compare masked zeros, indexed sparsity, structurally smaller rankers, and supported precision paths on the declared runtime.
concepts.evidence: Inspect metadata, conversion, actual lookup/kernel support, executed work, and complete timing; fewer payload bits do not automatically accelerate ranking.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a dense smaller model beat a sparser larger one?

concepts.experiment: Compare exact ordered compression combinations with the corresponding single transformations and unchanged complete request path.
concepts.evidence: Inspect compatible format support and matched combined outcomes; isolated savings cannot certify the combined new-item ranking behavior.
concepts.transfer_question: When would keeping only one transformation be preferable?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose a legal hardware mapping or host intervention using saved native traffic and complete-request evidence; reject the attractive local win that fails the endpoint goal and state a reversal condition.

concepts.experiment: For the declared dense-scoring region, compare arithmetic, bandwidth, and supported reuse interventions; show embedding-lookup supply separately.
concepts.evidence: Inspect the relevant workload/interface roofline and limiting regime rather than projecting dense-kernel peaks onto irregular lookup.
concepts.transfer_question: When would more arithmetic become preferable to a bandwidth intervention?

concepts.experiment: Step through supported stationary schedules for the dense ranking operator and count weight, activation, and partial-sum movement.
concepts.evidence: Compare operand traffic and supported movement-energy consequences; preserving one operand can increase another traffic class.
concepts.transfer_question: When would keeping activations resident be preferable to keeping weights resident?

concepts.experiment: Grow a supported scoring tile through the live-buffer and accumulator limit, then compare an aligned alternative and a fringe-producing shape.
concepts.evidence: Inspect legality, reuse, alignment, and fringe work; an illegal tile has no valid runtime.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a smaller tile outperform the largest legal one?

concepts.experiment: Carry the chosen legal improvement through feature gathering, embedding lookup, transfers, launches, scoring, eligibility, and filtering.
concepts.evidence: Compare complete request time and the newly binding stage; a dense-kernel improvement cannot remove untouched host work.
concepts.transfer_question: When would retaining the existing accelerator and repairing feature supply be preferable?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Write one bounded endpoint benchmark claim using saved protocol, uncertainty, operating-condition, and behavioral evidence; reject the broader headline and state what evidence could justify it.

concepts.experiment: Compare a warm fixed-candidate scoring claim with a complete request claim; repair timer endpoints, feature freshness, bundle identity, and included stages.
concepts.evidence: Inspect matched work and cold/warm conditions; scoring throughput alone does not establish shopper arrival-to-response latency.
concepts.transfer_question: When would the narrower scoring benchmark be the appropriate claim?

concepts.experiment: Allocate a fixed measurement budget between correlated requests and independent paired endpoint runs.
concepts.evidence: Inspect within-run and between-run variation and practical usefulness separately; repeated requests need not resolve uncertainty about a small improvement.
concepts.transfer_question: When would another independent run be more valuable than more requests in the same run?

concepts.experiment: Replay supported candidate/session mixtures, sustained demand conditions, and cold/warm feature states under the same benchmark contract.
concepts.evidence: Inspect full response tails, deadline misses, and declared energy window beside averages; fast stale-feature responses do not establish freshness.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a warm-only protocol adequately represent the stated use?

concepts.experiment: Lock relevance and new-item coverage obligations before revealing paired established/new-item and justified affected-population outcomes or supported calibration evidence. Inspect confidence calibration where task-supported and test a supplied repair on the same cases.
concepts.evidence: Inspect consequential differences hidden by aggregates and retain untested sessions as unknown; ranking quality is not proof of downstream commercial benefit. Preserve evidence counts and missing slices; a supported calibration repair need not change classifications.
concepts.transfer_question: When would requesting representative outcomes be preferable to tuning the aggregate score?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose a single-endpoint serving policy using saved complete-path, lost-service, batching, and live-state evidence; declare freshness separately and explain when another policy becomes preferable.

concepts.experiment: Compare supported host/model interventions on the same complete recommendation service path.
concepts.evidence: Inspect feature preparation, lookup, transfer, scoring, filtering, and response timing; keep catalog freshness separate from response duration.
concepts.transfer_question: When would feature-path repair be preferable to faster scoring?

concepts.experiment: Replay identical ranking-request arrivals at fixed admission under two supported single-endpoint service-capacity cases. Compare headroom before changing admission as an overload response.
concepts.evidence: Inspect utilization, backlog, and tail waiting as identical demand approaches available capacity. Then retain accepted/rejected work and latency denominators when admission changes; no fleet capacity is implied.
concepts.transfer_question: When would accepting longer waits be preferable to rejecting more requests?

concepts.experiment: Compare immediate dispatch with supported batching windows on identical request traces and candidate-shape constraints.
concepts.evidence: Inspect formation delay, realized batches, executed work, and missed deadlines; extra waiting may yield no executable batching benefit.
concepts.transfer_question: When would immediate dispatch outperform a throughput-oriented batching policy?

concepts.experiment: Cross and recover native embedding/model residency and per-request candidate/feature-buffer concurrency limits; inspect any language serving phases/KV comparison only in a separately named reference. In the separately labeled Language-serving reference, compare prefill/decode demands and a supported KV-limited concurrency change.
concepts.evidence: Distinguish persistent embedding tables from live ranking-request state; language KV observations establish no native ranker concurrency claim. Keep first-token delay, active-stream cadence, and KV residency separate from native task state.
concepts.transfer_question: When would lowering admitted concurrency be preferable to reducing candidate coverage?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose a release or recovery action using saved monitoring, parity, residency, and rollback evidence; identify a rejected response and the new evidence that would reverse your decision.

concepts.experiment: Choose feature/freshness, exposure, or outcome monitoring and replay early signals followed by delayed attributed feedback.
concepts.evidence: Inspect alert sensitivity, confirmation delay, and investigation cost; stable endpoint health or an exposure warning alone does not establish discovery outcomes.
concepts.transfer_question: When would waiting for targeted outcomes be preferable to retraining immediately?

concepts.experiment: Compare request-keyed transformed features and rankings under immutable model, embedding vocabulary, feature schema/snapshot, and runtime identities; repair a supplied mismatch.
concepts.evidence: Inspect paired values rather than only aggregate distributions; identical version labels or similar distributions can conceal request-level disagreement.
concepts.transfer_question: When would aggregate monitoring suffice for the limited claim being made?

concepts.experiment: Change canary exposure while reserving complete baseline and candidate ranking bundles, then choose a feasible staged or held transition.
concepts.evidence: Inspect model/embedding copies, live state, evidence strength, and exposure separately; small traffic share does not make a candidate copy proportionally smaller.
concepts.transfer_question: When would sequential staging be preferable to concurrent canarying?

concepts.experiment: Try reverting only scorer weights after an incompatible refresh, then restore the supported compatible feature/embedding/model/runtime bundle; compare a real population shift.
concepts.evidence: Inspect request-keyed recovery and freshness/outcome limits; containment is not verified recovery, and rollback cannot erase a changed population.
concepts.transfer_question: When would restricting service and gathering new evidence be preferable to rollback?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Recommend a responsible service scope or hold using saved goal, mitigation, feedback, and lifecycle evidence; identify the rejected alternative and a condition that would change your recommendation.

concepts.experiment: State useful discovery and affected-seller obligations. On the same supplied audited recommendations with different relevance base rates, compare exposure parity with equal opportunity for relevant products; justify the criterion.
concepts.evidence: Inspect seller-group counts, base rates, click proxy versus independent discovery evidence, and criterion-dependent pass/fail/insufficient gates with recommendations fixed. Exposure-conditioned missing outcomes remain unknown.
concepts.transfer_question: When would changing the justified fairness criterion reverse a release verdict without changing the recommendations?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported exposure/coverage or ranking interventions against the same declared obligations and matched relevance/resource evidence.
concepts.evidence: Inspect distinct error consequences and mitigation costs without a universal fairness slider; one improved aggregate cannot offset a failed stated obligation.
concepts.transfer_question: When would restricting scope be preferable to the available mitigation?

concepts.experiment: Compare exposure-conditioned click collection with a supported representative audit policy, then test a cause-specific response using supplied independent outcomes.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which products or sellers remain unobserved and the cost of obtaining independent evidence; the endpoint influences which labels exist.
concepts.transfer_question: When would paying for an audit be preferable to retraining on more clicks?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported lifecycle alternatives at equal useful recommendation service, including preparation, refresh, training, and endpoint operation within declared boundaries.
concepts.evidence: Inspect dollars, energy, and emissions separately, retaining excluded or unsourced terms as unknown; cheaper operation need not mean lower lifecycle emissions.
concepts.transfer_question: When would higher operating cost be justified by the declared lifecycle obligation?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Defend release, restricted scope, baseline/fallback, or hold for this exact recommendation endpoint; cite compatible saved evidence, reject an alternative, name the next decisive test, and specify the change that would reopen the decision.

concepts.experiment: Audit a proposed release dossier and accept, replay, or reject records by requirement, interaction/session data, feature snapshot, embeddings, ranker, runtime, benchmark, and operating identity.
concepts.evidence: Inspect compatible support and missing links rather than counting completed labs; one project name does not make mismatched artifacts composable.
concepts.transfer_question: When would replaying an old comparison be preferable to gathering a wholly new one?

concepts.experiment: Carry one previously supported candidate improvement through the complete ranking path and compare it with its rejected alternative under the same contract.
concepts.evidence: Inspect joint resource fit, relevance, new-item coverage, freshness, and service evidence; local wins and individually passing records need not compose.
concepts.transfer_question: When would retaining the baseline be preferable to the apparently improved bundle?

concepts.experiment: Tighten a supported request-demand, memory, freshness, or coverage obligation without changing the saved consumption observations.
concepts.evidence: Inspect where the chosen bundle ceases to qualify and compare familiar recovery, restriction, or hold options; a policy limit changes acceptability rather than historical measurements.
concepts.transfer_question: Which smallest changed requirement would make your rejected alternative preferable?

concepts.experiment: Apply a supported feature-path or population change and identify which prior claims expire before testing a familiar cause-specific response.
concepts.evidence: Inspect physical feasibility separately from behavioral validity; single-endpoint evidence does not establish fleet readiness or guaranteed commercial benefit.
concepts.transfer_question: When would revising the supported population be preferable to restoring an older bundle?

provenance.numerical_status: Intended experiments; matched numerical fixtures and observed outcome evidence require separate implementation and validation.
